claim: Google Cloud Workbench instances (notebook/agent execution VMs) default to shutting down after 180 minutes of inactivity.
stance_target: auto-killing idle agents is a documented production pattern
scope_conditions: Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Workbench instances
quoted_support: Idle shutdown is enabled and set to shut down your instance after 180 inactive minutes by default.

claim: Idle shutdown activity detection is defined narrowly as kernel API activity, not raw CPU usage, meaning a compute-bound but non-interactive process does not prevent termination.
stance_target: quiet self-termination requires a precise health-check / activity-signal definition
quoted_support: CPU usage doesn't reset the idle shutdown timer. ... idle shutdown looks for activity in kernels running in the following addresses of the instance: 127.0.0.1:8080/api/sessions, /api/terminals, /api/kernels

claim: Idle shutdown is configured via a single metadata key (idle-timeout-seconds) settable through gcloud CLI or Terraform, making it infrastructure-as-code friendly.

Billing for idle-shutdown instances drops CPU/GPU charges while shut down but retains disk storage charges, and scheduled executions still fire on schedule even while the instance is nominally shut down.
stance_target: cost model of idle/dormant agent infrastructure
quoted_support: While your instance is shut down, there are no CPU or GPU usage charges except for scheduled executions that run during the shutdown. ... If you have scheduled an execution of a notebook file in a Agent Platform Workbench instance that is shut down, the execution still runs on schedule.
